'''Dionigi Galletto''' (26 January 1932 – 25 September 2011) was an Italian [[mathematician]] and [[academician]].

He is known for his work on [[Rigid body dynamics|rigid body mechanics]], on the mathematical theory of elasticity (including both [[linear elasticity]] and [[finite strain theory]]), on the [[history of mathematics]] and on [[cosmology]] and extragalactic [[celestial mechanics]]: in particular he is considered one of the founders of the latter branch of cosmology.<ref>In [[#{{harvid|Вујановић|2012}}|Vujanović's words (2012]], p. 669), "Проф. Галето се сматра оснивачем екстрагалактичке небеске механике." ({{langx|en|"Prof. Galletto is the founder of extragalactic celestial mechanics"}}).</ref>

He was professor of mathematical physics at the [[University of Turin]]:<ref>{{harv|Pastrone|2012|p=80}}. See also to [[#{{harvid|Accademia delle Scienze di Torino|2013}}|his member data]] available at the Accademia delle Scienze di Torino online.</ref> as such, he is considered to be the founder–reorganiser of the [[Mathematical physics]] school of Turin in the Post–[[Second World War]] period.<ref>According to Franco Pastrone as recorded in {{harv|Borgi|2012}}.</ref> Among his students was [[Mauro Francaviglia]].

==Biography==

He started his university studies in [[Rome]] as a student of [[Francesco Severi|Severi]]: however his studies were interrupted due to the military service, which led him to [[Padua]].<ref name="mpg" >According to the obituary {{harv|m.p.g.|2011}}.</ref> There he graduated with honours in 1960 under [[Giuseppe Grioli]]'s guidance, with a thesis on the [[continuum mechanics|continuum theory with asymmetric stress]]: from 1961 to 1968 he worked in Padua as an [[associate professor]],<ref name="mpg" /><ref name="Vujanović.669" >See also {{harv|Вујановић|2012|p=669}}.</ref> holding also courses on [[differential geometry]] as a [[lecturer]].<ref name="BarbieriTaddeip178">According to his biography, as reported by {{harvtxt|Barbieri|Taddei|2006|p=178}}.</ref>

In 1968, having won a competitive examination for a chair in [[Classical mechanics|rational mechanics]], he was appointed [[extraordinary professor]] of [[Classical mechanics|rational mechanics]] at the [[University of Palermo]]:<ref>See {{harv|m.p.g.|2011}} and {{harv|Barbieri|Taddei|2006|p=178}}. {{harv|Barbieri|Taddei|2006|p=178}} report precisely that his position was "professore straordinario" of "meccanica razionale".</ref> there, Galletto held also courses of mathematical methods for physicists as a lecturer.<ref name="BarbieriTaddeip178" /> In 1970 he moved to the University of Turin, working at the Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Natural Sciences again as extraordinary professor of [[higher mechanics]]:<ref>Precisely, he was appointed as professor of "Meccanica superiore", according to {{harv|m.p.g.|2011}} and to {{harvtxt|Barbieri|Taddei|2006|p=178}} who report also his exact position.</ref> in 1971 he became [[full professor]] of mathematical physics, a position he held up to 2007, when he retired. Besides the course of mathematical physics, Galletto held various courses relating to the area of his scientific interest: for example he held courses on astronomy as a lecturer.<ref name="BarbieriTaddeip178" /> In 2008 he was appointed [[Emeritus professor]].

===Honors===
In 1965 he was awarded the [[Ottorino Pomini prize]] by the [[Unione Matematica Italiana]], jointly with [[Giuseppe Geymonat]] and [[Mario Miranda (mathematician)|Mario Miranda]]: the judging commission was composed by [[Dario Graffi]] (as the president), [[Giuseppe Grioli]], [[Ennio De Giorgi]] and [[Enzo Martinelli]] (as the secretary).<ref name="Pomini"/>

He was [[corresponding member]] of the [[Accademia delle Scienze di Torino]] since 1974, and became national resident member in 1980.<ref name="Pastrone.80">{{harv|Pastrone|2012|p=80}}.</ref><ref name="Vujanović.669" /><ref>According to [[#{{harvid|Accademia delle Scienze di Torino|2013}}|his member data]], he was elected "''Socio corrispondente''" on March 13, 1974, and "''Socio nazionale residente''" on May 5, 1980.</ref>

In 1979 he was elected corresponding member of the [[Accademia Nazionale di Scienze, Lettere e Arti di Modena]]:<ref name="Pastrone.80" /> later on, he became effective member in 1984 and emeritus member in 2002.<ref name="BarbieriTaddeip178" /> He was also corresponding member of the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]].<ref name="Pastrone.80" />

Since 1980 he was corresponding member of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]], and was elected national member in 1990.<ref>According to the [[#{{harvid|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei|2012}}|Lincean yearbook (2012, p. 460]]), he was elected "''membro corrispondente''" on August 5, 1980, and "''membro nazionale''" on December 6, 1990.</ref><ref name="Pastrone.80" /><ref name="Vujanović.669" /> In 1989, the same academy awarded him the "''[[Ministry of Cultural Heritage and Activities (Italy)|Prize of the Minister of Heritage and Cultural Activity]]''" for his work in mathematics and mechanics.<ref>Precisely, he was awarded the "''Premio del Ministro per i Beni Culturali e Ambientali''", according to the [[#{{harvid|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei|2012}}|Lincean yearbook (2012, p. 153]]).</ref><ref name="Pastrone.80" />

On November 2, 2006 he was elected member of the [[Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts]],<ref name="Pastrone.80" /><ref>([[#{{harvid|САНУ|2015}}|САНУ Yearbook 2015,]] p. 60).</ref> and few months later, on 7 March 2007, he was elected corresponding non resident member to the class of mathematical sciences of the [[Società Nazionale di Scienze Lettere e Arti in Napoli]].<ref name="Pastrone.80" /><ref>See the [[#{{harvid|Società Nazionale di Scienze Lettere e Arti in Napoli|2014}}|Society yearbook (2014]], p. 40).</ref>

==Work==

===Research activity===
During his career, he published more than 150 papers in Italian and international journals.<ref name="mpg" /> The beginning of his scientific production was under Grioli's scientific influence: Galletto worked on the topic of his [[laurea]] thesis, i.e. on the theory of continua having asymmetric stress characteristics. However, soon he followed his independent research path, with pioneering works that forerun the so called generalised continuum theory. In this theory, among other things, the stress tensor considered is no longer the [[Cauchy stress tensor|Cauchy tensor]] or any similar, double [[symmetric tensor]], but an asymmetric tensor that  generalizes it: and this gives to the theory many further important structural peculiarities.

}}. This is a [[monograph]]ic [[Serial (literature)|fascicle]] published on the "Bollettino della Unione Matematica Italiana", describing the history of the "Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi" from its foundation in 1939 to 2003: it was written by [[Gino Roghi]] and includes a presentation by Salvatore Coen and a preface by Corrado De Concini. It is almost exclusively based on [[source text|sources]] from the institute archives: the wealth and variety of materials included, jointly with its [[Addendum#In books|appendices]] and [[Index (publishing)|indexes]], make this monograph a useful reference not only for the history of the [[institute]] itself, but also for the history of many [[mathematician]]s who taught or followed the institute courses or simply worked there.
